posts.headline: He started with pocket money. Now he has served *10 million free meals*
posts.body: In 2016, pharmacy student Mohd Sujathullah fed hungry strangers at Secunderabad Railway Station. Today his Humanity First Foundation serves breakfast outside Hyderabad's government hospitals every morning, and he runs a hospital for people who can't afford care.
posts.source: The Logical Indian, The Better India
posts.caption:
It began with a few food packets bought with a student's pocket money. 🍲

In 2016, Mohd Sujathullah, then a 22-year-old pharmacy student, saw people going hungry at Secunderabad Railway Station and decided to feed them. A decade later, his Humanity First Foundation has served more than 10 million free meals, with breakfast handed out every morning outside government hospitals in Hyderabad. He has also set up Humanity Hospital to help people who can't afford treatment.

One small act, repeated every day for 10 years. 💛

posts.headline: From 36 schools to *6.26 lakh students*: Ashok Leyland's Road to School
posts.sub: How a truck maker's foundation is helping children in government schools learn, stay and grow.

slides.title: 2015: *36 government schools* in Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu
slides.body: Ashok Leyland started Road to School near its plants with its partner NGO, Learning Links Foundation, to close learning gaps in rural government schools.

slides.title: Reading, maths, health, sports and *art*
slides.body: The programme supports foundational literacy and numeracy, wellness sessions, structured sports and creative learning, and works with parents and communities to keep children in school.

slides.title: Now across *9 states* and 25 districts
slides.body: Since 2022, Road to Livelihood also helps students in Classes 9 to 12 with digital skills, spoken English and career guidance. The goal: 10 lakh students.

posts.takeaway: When a company invests in classrooms, *a whole generation* gets a better start.
posts.source: India CSR, Ashok Leyland, Autocar Professional
posts.caption:
From 36 schools to more than 6 lakh students. 📚

In 2015, Ashok Leyland Foundation began Road to School with Learning Links Foundation in 36 government schools in Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu. Today it reaches 6.26 lakh students in 4,585 government schools across 9 states, with support for reading, maths, health, sports and art. Its Road to Livelihood programme now helps older students get ready for college and jobs.

posts.stat_label: given by Indian companies to education in FY 2023-24
posts.headline: Education is India Inc's *biggest good-work* priority
points: Total social-good spending: ₹34,909 crore in FY 2023-24
posts.source: Ministry of Corporate Affairs (PIB, National CSR Data Portal)
posts.caption:
More than ₹12,000 crore for classrooms in one year. 🎓

In FY 2023-24, Indian companies spent ₹34,909 crore on social good, and education got the biggest share at ₹12,134 crore. That total has more than tripled from ₹10,066 crore in FY 2014-15, and 27,188 companies contributed in FY 2023-24.

posts.headline: How a woman sarpanch helped her village win *India's first climate award*
posts.sub: Dawwa in Gondia, Maharashtra, chose trees, solar power and people-led change.

slides.title: Yogeshwari Chaudhary, *Dawwa's first woman sarpanch*
slides.body: A schoolteacher from Dawwa in Sadak Arjuni taluka, Gondia, she stepped up to lead her village through long gram sabha meetings and decisions taken together.

slides.title: Solar power, mixed crops and *greener habits*
slides.body: Farmers tried solar irrigation, women's self-help groups joined decisions, and waste was turned into compost for kitchen gardens.

slides.title: First in India to win the *Climate Action Special Panchayat Award*
slides.body: Dawwa Gram Panchayat won the award at the National Panchayat Awards 2023-24, along with a ₹1 crore prize.

posts.takeaway: Big climate change can start with *one village* that decides to act together.
posts.caption:
A small village in Gondia just showed India how climate action is done. 🌱

Under Yogeshwari Chaudhary, its first woman sarpanch, Dawwa in Maharashtra planted more than 1,16,000 trees, brought in solar power and got farmers and women's self-help groups making decisions together. The result: Dawwa Gram Panchayat became the first in India to win the Climate Action Special Panchayat Award, with a ₹1 crore prize.
